description: Cyclone Gezani caused widespread devastation in Madagascar. More than 30 people died after Cyclone Gezani struck, causing widespread destruction in Toamasina, the island's second-largest city, according to authorities. At least 36 people were reported seriously injured. More than 2,740 residents were evacuated as a precaution after the cyclone battered coastal communities before moving inland. According to the BNGRC, the cyclone displaced approximately 6,870 people, while a total of 250,406 were classified as victims of the disaster.

description: Tropical Cyclone Fytia made landfall in Madagascar on January 31, causing widespread flooding in northwestern Madagascar. Nearly 18,600 houses were flooded, damaged, or destroyed, while 493 classrooms and 20 health facilities sustained damage.

Continued rainfall since the initial flooding has compounded damage, displacement and humanitarian needs, while river overflow, notably along the Licungo River, has further exacerbated impacts in affected areas.

While some affected families have been able to return to their areas of origin, many remain displaced due to ongoing rainfall, damaged or unsafe housing, loss of assets, and limited access to essential services.

In mid-December, severe and prolonged flooding affected large parts of southern and central Mozambique. Rivers burst their banks, displacing communities and damaging or destroying homes, health facilities, water systems and other critical infrastructure. The National Institute for Disaster Management and Risk Reduction reports that more than 724,000 people have been affected by floods. At the peak of the emergency, over 100,000 people were hosted in approximately 100
accommodation centres.
